brief.query: root opening 0.8 mm on 2 mm sheet steel fillet weld: maximum root gap allowed before backing or buildup is required, and how to correct sheet metal fit-up that opens along the joint
brief.headline: Seam too wide for single-pass bridge on 2mm stainless
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations, the seam opened wider than one pass can bridge. The widest measured 0.75 mm on 2 mm sheet. The cell refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: [1] Recommends maximum root gap for fillet welds is 1 mm, absolute max 1.5 mm on stainless. [2] AWS D1.1 5.22.4.3 allows root openings up to 20 mm (3/4 in) to be corrected by welding to acceptable dimensions prior to joining, but requires engineer approval if exceeding standard limits.
do_now: Measure the actual gap at the 20 stations with a feeler gauge and record the exact spread
Grind the high spots on the sheet edges to reduce the gap to no more than 1.0 mm before welding
If gap remains above 1.0 mm, prepare a repair pass on the sheet edge to bring it within the 1.0 mm limit
Re-check the gap with a feeler gauge after grinding to confirm it is within the 1.0 mm maximum

brief.query: root opening 1.5 mm on 2 mm sheet steel fillet weld: maximum root gap allowed before backing or buildup is required, and how to correct sheet metal fit-up that opens along the joint
brief.headline: Seam too wide for single-pass bridge at 20 stations
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations the seam opening exceeded one-pass bridging capacity; the widest measured 1.50 mm on 2 mm sheet. The cell refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: Welding instructions for stainless steel recommend a maximum root gap of 1.5 mm for fillet welds [1]. AWS D1.1 permits root openings up to 3/16" (approximately 5 mm) for plates, with correction allowed up to twice the thinner part thickness or 20 mm, whichever is less [3].
do_now: Measure the actual gap at the 20 refused stations with a feeler gauge
Grind down high spots on the sheet edges to reduce the gap to 1.0 mm or less
Re-track the seam at the corrected stations and verify the gap is bridgeable
If gap remains above 1.5 mm, plan multi-pass welding or joint redesign

brief.topic: joint opened too far to weld
brief.query: root opening 3.8 mm on 2 mm sheet steel fillet weld: maximum root gap allowed before backing or buildup is required, and how to correct sheet metal fit-up that opens along the joint
brief.headline: Seam too wide at 20 stations on 2 mm sheet, robot refused pass
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations, the seam opened wider than one pass can bridge. The widest measured 3.75 mm on 2 mm sheet. The robot refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: AWS D1.1 5.22.4.3 allows root openings greater than 5.22.4.1 but not greater than twice the thickness of the thinner part or 3/4 in. [20 mm], whichever is less, and may be corrected by welding to acceptable dimensions prior to joining [1]. Eng-Tips discussion notes that for fillet welds, gaps can be reduced by buttering, and gaps up to 1/16" (approx 1.6 mm) may not require weld size increase; larger gaps may need engineer approval [2][3]. Maximum allowed root gap for fillet welds is recommended 1 mm, max 1.5 mm [3].
do_now: Grind the widest seam points down to 1.5 mm or less before re-tracking
Re-track the seam at the four worst stations and verify gap is under 1.5 mm
If gap remains above 1.5 mm, stop and request engineer approval for weld build-up per AWS 5.22.4.3 [1]
Run a test bead on a scrap piece of 2 mm sheet at the corrected gap to confirm bridging is possible
brief.caveat: Sources do not specify a maximum gap for single-pass bridging on 2 mm sheet; the 1.5 mm recommendation from source [3] is the only quantitative limit available.

brief.headline: Seam too wide for single pass at 20 stations on 2 mm stainless
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations the seam opened wider than one pass can bridge; the widest measured 1.25 mm on 2 mm sheet. The cell refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: Welding instructions for stainless steel recommend maximum root gap of 1 mm, absolute max 1.5 mm [1]. AWS D1.1 permits root openings greater than 5.22.4.1 but not greater than 3/4 in [20 mm] or twice the thinner part thickness, whichever is less, and correction by welding to acceptable dimensions prior to joining is allowed [2]. For fillet welds, gaps can be reduced by buttering, and gap dimension may be added to fillet weld leg size up to 3/16" [3].
do_now: Grind the widest seam openings at the 20 stations to reduce gap to 1.0 mm or less
Verify all 20 stations now measure 1.0 mm gap or less before proceeding
If any station still exceeds 1.0 mm, apply buttering passes to the edge to build up the gap to within 1.0 mm
Re-measure all 20 stations to confirm gap is within 1.0 mm before welding

brief.query: root opening 2.8 mm on 2 mm sheet steel fillet weld: maximum root gap allowed before backing or buildup is required, and how to correct sheet metal fit-up that opens along the joint
brief.headline: Root opening exceeds single-pass bridge capacity on 2mm sheet
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations, root openings were too wide for a single pass; the widest measured 2.75 mm on 2 mm sheet. The cell refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: AWS D1.1 limits root opening to 3/4" (19 mm) for prequalified WPS; wider openings require engineer approval [1][3]. Fillet weld root gap max is 1 mm recommended, 1.5 mm absolute [3]. Gap beyond 1/16" requires weld leg increase or engineer demo of effective throat [4].
do_now: Measure the actual root opening at the 20 refused stations with a feeler gauge
Grind the largest openings down to 1.5 mm or less before attempting a single-pass bead
If any opening remains above 1.5 mm, stop and seek engineer approval before welding
Document the ground-down dimensions and update the fit-up record
brief.caveat: Sources do not specify the exact material thickness at the refused stations beyond the 2 mm sheet reference; the 1.5 mm grind limit comes from general fillet weld gap recommendations, not a direct match to the 2.75 mm measured value.

brief.headline: Seam too wide for single pass on 2 mm sheet at 20 stations
brief.what_the_cell_measured: At 20 stations the seam opened wider than one pass can bridge; the widest measured 4.25 mm on 2 mm sheet. The cell refused those stations rather than laying a bead across them.
brief.what_the_sources_say: AWS D1.1 5.22.4.3 permits root openings greater than 5.22.4.1 but not greater than twice the thickness of the thinner part or 20 mm [3/4 in.], whichever is less, and may be corrected by welding to acceptable dimensions prior to joining [1]. Eng-Tips discussion notes that for fillet welds, gaps can be reduced by buttering and if gap reduced to 1/16" or less no need to increase weld size; buttering to reduce root opening in groove welds is common practice [3][4].
do_now: Measure each of the 20 stations with a feeler gauge and record the actual gap
Grind back the largest gaps on the 2 mm sheet to reduce root opening to 1.5 mm or less per AWS recommendation [3]
If gaps remain above 1.5 mm after grinding, stop and seek engineer approval before proceeding [1][5]
Re-track the seam to verify all stations now meet the reduced gap limit
brief.caveat: Sources do not specify the exact maximum gap a single pass can bridge for 2 mm sheet; engineer sign-off may be required if gaps exceed 1.5 mm after grinding [1][5]
